title: Fix color contrast
when: Text or controls are hard to read, a check reports low contrast, or the user wants colors to meet WCAG AA.
prompt:
Goal: Every text and background pair reaches 4.5 to 1 (3 to 1 for large text and UI parts) while keeping the brand feel.
Steps:
1. List each foreground and background pair in use: body text, muted text, links, buttons, placeholders, disabled states, text on images.
2. Compute each ratio with the WCAG formula from relative luminance; mark pairs under 4.5 to 1.
3. Fix by darkening the text or lightening the background in the same hue; adjust lightness, keep hue and saturation close.
4. For brand colors too light for text, keep them for fills and borders and add a darker text variant (--brand-ink).
5. Text on photos gets a solid or gradient scrim behind it.
6. Store the fixed colors as custom properties on :root and replace hard coded values.
Quality bar:
- Muted text still reaches 4.5 to 1.
- Focus rings and input borders reach 3 to 1.
- Links are distinguishable without color alone (underline).
Pitfalls:
- Light gray placeholder text as the only hint.
- Checking only the default state, not hover and disabled.
- Using opacity on text, which lowers contrast unpredictably.
Verify:
- [ ] Each text pair in the CSS reaches 4.5 to 1.
- [ ] Colors come from custom properties.
- [ ] Links are underlined or otherwise marked.
- [ ] Dark mode pairs are checked too if present.
Output: The updated stylesheet with a table of old and new pairs and their ratios.

examples.input: o texto cinza está difícil de ler
examples.output: #9aa0a6 on white (2.6:1) changed to #5f6368 (6.3:1); brand yellow kept for fills only
